about: Coefficients of friction by pair of materials, for a contact set whose
FrictionFrom is Materials (docs/AssemblyDynamics.md, P6). A component's
material card is in the first family one of whose words its name, its
KindOfMaterial or one of its tags holds, ignoring case; a component with
no card, or one in no family, and a pair not listed here, run on the set's
own StaticFriction and DynamicFriction. Engineering values, for parts in
air -- not clean and dry, which for metals run two to three times higher.
Where a source gives one coefficient it is the static one, and the dynamic
is five sixths of it, the ratio of the sets' defaults (0.30 / 0.25); where
it gives a range, its low end. Restitution stays the set's: it depends on
the speed more than on the pair.
A file of the same form at <user data>/Assembly/ContactFriction.json is
read over this one: its families are tried first, its pairs replace these.

sources.deulin: E. A. Deulin, V. P. Mikhailov, Yu. V. Panfilov, R. A. Nevshupa, Mechanics and Physics of Precise Vacuum Mechanisms: friction in air, as tabulated in tribonet.org, 'Friction coefficients in air vs vacuum' (read 2026-11-03)
